component.name: PirateFinder
component.summary: Find Amiga and Atari ST menu disks and write them to floppy

description.p: PirateFinder keeps a searchable catalogue of what is on the numbered menu disks, compacts and packs released by Amiga and Atari ST crews such as Automation, Pompey Pirates, Medway Boys and D-Bug, together with single-game cracks. Search for a game, a crew or a disk number and the results show which disks carry it.

Chosen disks are found in local or network folders, or downloaded on request from public online archives and checked against the catalogue hash. PirateFinder prepares each image and writes it to a real floppy with a Greaseweazle, reporting progress for every disk and a summary at the end. The Greaseweazle host tools are included.
More discs found, and more ways to spell a title.

ul.li: A sequel number finds its title in Roman or Arabic numerals, so "Turrican 2" and "Turrican II" find the same discs
A word with letters and digits in it, such as "turrican2", finds its title, and names are found with or without the space between two words
A name that begins with a crew's short alias finds titles under the alias and under the full name
scene.org and Fujiology are download providers, each with its own switch in Preferences
LZH files are read, in library folders and as downloads, so the Vectronix disks can be downloaded from the Vectronix CD on the Internet Archive once the next catalogue lists them
An MSA image with one track record more than its header declares is read, as several on the Vectronix CD are
A download no checksum could check, and a copy cleaned of a boot block virus, stay with their disc in the library, also after a catalogue update
The bundled catalogue locates thousands more discs, from newer TOSEC sets on the Internet Archive and from Demozoo's download links, and names the crew of most Amiga discs that had none

description.p: Pictures a busy site turned away are asked for again.

ul.li: A picture a site says it does not have is asked for again an hour later, and a cached copy is kept meanwhile; only a second such answer in a row leaves it out for seven days
Download All Pictures rests a site that misses picture after picture, and asks once more at the end for every picture it missed

description.p: Pictures ahead of time, and a steadier application update.

ul.li: Download All Pictures in Preferences fetches every picture the catalogue lists for the Atari ST, the Amiga or both, so the details pane never waits for one
Installing an application update waits for the password prompt however long it stays open

description.p: A new Find screen and a details pane.

ul.li: Filters for platform, type, crew, year and disc kind, one search box for every field, and results as titles or discs, sorted and paged
A details pane with the disc, its release date, the other titles on it, pictures, crew histories and trivia
Boot block viruses found on Amiga and Atari ST discs, removed before writing or cleaned from the stored image
Downloads checked against every known dump of the disc and filed by platform, type and crew
Corrections to a disc's details that survive catalogue updates
Optional IPF support, installed after its licence is accepted
Packages for Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 on amd64, arm64 and armhf
Check for Application Updates in the About window, which downloads, checks and installs a newer version
An illustrated User Guide in the Help menu
